corrections: Neither dump establishes statewide first occupation11,500BCE or universal first coastal-bayou settlement afterAD1. Mehta2019 concerns Grand Caillou/Lafourche, not Paleoindian Louisiana.
Page-Ladson is Florida; Cooper’s Ferry Idaho; Hester Mississippi; Wapanocca Arkansas; Cedros/Faro Mexico; Dor an Israel comparison. Regional context is not a Louisiana dated settlement.
Hillman components do not establish uninterruptedAD1–1000 occupation. Cultural-period endpoints are not site founding/abandonment dates.
Landform emergence/OSL age is not occupation. Delta abandonment and truncation of dated activity may coincide without proving a single cause.
Saunders1997 seasonal use differs from2005 all-season basal evidence. Plants later domesticated are not thereby already proven crops at Watson Brake.
Watson Brake construction continued sometime after3000BCE. No hard3000BCE endpoint invented; ca3500BCE onset plotted as rounded reference only.
Trubitt2019 and Kassabaum2012 are book reviews. Zejdlik review is unrelated. Pringle1997 is news about the Science report, not independent excavation.
Girard1999 belongs to archaeological Caddoan literature/SFA ITA, not Theoretical Informatics and Applications. Belcher mound and Comegys village remain distinct.
Helmer online2022 is Holocene33(3)2023; Dor online2021 is Quaternary Research105(2022); Mehta online2025 appears in2026issue45(1).
Automated method labels, citation counts and rankings are not scientific confidence. Artifacts, mounds, rooms, genetic effective population and core ages are not resident totals.

unresolved: Numerical public archaeological coordinates not verified for Paradise Wes-15a, Sweetwater Wes-15b or White Marl. Keep separate named records unmapped; tourist, school, town and property centroids are not substitutes.
No present-day exhaustive survey inventory established. Callaghan 2008 and Rampersad 2009 describe publication-era knowledge; no proof of pre-5000 cal BP nonoccupation.
Paradise Table 1 has disjoint ranges and later charcoal beginning 1312; narrative shorthand sometimes says 1390. Table retained; later cultural attribution unresolved.

Elliott abstract/conclusion calls the after-670 cal BP phase European colonization, but 670 cal BP is about AD 1280. Results distinguish later sugarcane after about 440 cal BP and upper plow disturbance. Do not equate that phase boundary with European arrival.
JFA 2008 book-list row lacks issue, author and DOI. Exact entry unresolved; no field claims extracted.
White Marl tentative cacao and possible nonlocal individual require corroboration/baselines. No confirmed first cacao or migration route.
Blue Marlin cultural-period chronology is not every site occupation. DeWolf sites need direct contextual chronology review before adding dated records.
No resident population totals follow from sherd percentages, burials, midden area or title duration. No population estimate assigned.
corrections: Reported absence is not demonstrated absence of people. Categorical no-pre-5000-cal-BP conclusion and inconsistent 500 BCE threshold not adopted.
Rampersad explicitly reported lack of comprehensive coastline survey in 2009; extensive exhaustive island surveys are not established.
Callaghan rough-seas and large-canoe explanation is a hypothesis, not proven cause.
Paradise Table 1: charcoal 673–778/785–838, shell 710–896, later charcoal 1312–1362/1386–1428 cal AD. Combined envelope is not continuous occupation or one ceramic tradition.
Sweetwater charcoal 1396–1466 cal AD is a sample range, not foundation/abandonment dates; post-contact activity separately open-ended.
White Marl village 1050–450 cal BP = approximately AD 900–1500, around 600 years. 1300-year land-use legacy is not 1300 years uninterrupted village life.
Three White Marl burials collectively span cal AD 1221–1641; late burial does not extend continuous village life through 1641.
97% concerns 75 sampled sherds and clay provenance, not all pottery production. Imported vessels versus distant clay procurement remain interpretations; exports unquantified.
Cacao identification tentative. Different sediment and calculus proxies yield different plants; absence in one proxy does not prove crop absence.
Hackenberger concerns Barbuda; Kraan Curaçao. Fitzpatrick around 7000 cal BP is not 7000 BCE.
Oliver is book review; JFA bibliographic listing. DeWolf regional framework is not four demonstrated Jamaican populations.
Publication versions retained: Oxford 2017 versus supplied 2016; Mickleburgh online 2018/issue 2019; Elliott online 2022/issue 2024; Public Archaeology volume 2022/online 2023.
Consensus meters, citations and automated method labels are not evidence-quality measures. Working intake only; no website deployment or shared dataset mutation.

unresolved.reason: Exact public archaeological coordinates for Bellows O18 and Faʻahia remain unverified. Sear publishes a lake coordinate, not an ancient settlement. Broad schematic regional anchors now make the evidence viewable without substituting exact site points.
Ioannidis 2021 extended model tables and numerical confidence intervals were not independently audited. Point estimates remain in qualified claim text; no padded timeline ranges are invented.
Marquesan and Society hypotheses remain alternatives. Neither genomic network sampling nor chronological compatibility identifies an exclusive first Hawaiian homeland.
Biomarkers, archaeological basal layers, site-establishment posteriors and regional colonization models target different events and should not be silently collapsed.
Preserve full model definitions and calibration assumptions if recomputing; 67% and 95% HPDs cannot be exchanged or treated as occupation cores.
No original experimental-voyage report was supplied or independently audited here. Capability experiments can test viability but do not directly date prehistoric arrivals.
Tice item, Brown review venue, Jacobeit exact identity, alleged Emory2016 edition and Glick electronic/original edition date remain unresolved; no prehistoric claims rely on them.

Broad export assertions about forest clearance, rats, flightless bird extinction and agricultural infrastructure require dedicated source-specific dates and causal studies. No automatic all-island contemporaneity inferred.

Austronesian and Polynesian language relationships must be modeled separately from genetic ancestry, archaeological traditions and named peoples. Ioannidis background citations alone do not date a single Taiwan-to-Hawaiʻi migration.

corrections.correction: Ioannidis 2021 did not sample Hawaiʻi. It cannot directly trace the first Hawaiian colonists or date their arrival.
Athens2014 940–1130 CE (95% HPD) and 1000–1100 CE (67% HPD), Dye2011 variants, and Wilmshurst2011 1219–1266 CE differ. Preserve source-specific models and methodological debate.
Online December2010, issue February2011. Regional phase estimates are not precise dates for all islands, and Mulrooney2011 challenges selection/statistics; Wilmshurst2011 reply defends them.

Atiu is in the Southern Cook Islands. Pig/human biomarkers are indirect local indicators rather than direct Hawaiian arrival evidence. Erratum adds Emma Pearson and funding acknowledgment without changing dates.
Environmental stress is a proposed contributory explanation, not established motive for every voyage or proof of an actual modeled route.
About1050–1160 CE concerns the investigated lowest cultural layer and 12 short-lived determinations, not every Society Island or a known Hawaiian departure event.
Allen separates secure, probable and less-secure chronology evidence and retains homeland uncertainty; do not declare Marquesan origin proven.
The inspected abstract supports distinct settlement-process models, not Hawaiian settlement5000years ago.
These are book reviews; Petersen2019 is not the author of Kirch’s archaeological history, and neither review is a new primary dating program.
Travel writing, German implement inventory and an education perspective do not provide the prehistoric archaeology/experimental methods assigned to them by the export.
A 1959 Origin of the Hawaiians is bibliographically documented; the export’s2016 attribution is unresolved.
Related language families, modeled ancestry and archaeological traditions are distinct evidence. No one-to-one language–gene–people equivalence adopted.

corrections.correction: The matching title is Barton and Harvey (2000), mammalian brain evolution, not evidence for Micronesian/Polynesian origins.

corrections.target: Hudjashov used as original phonological evidence
corrections.correction: Hudjashov 2018 is a genomic study. Wilson 2012 supplies the primary abstract's 73 lexical/grammatical innovation claim; the input's over-200 phonological count is not adopted.
mtDNA coalescence, present-day admixture dates, rat genealogy, archaeological sample ages and inferred language splits are distinct quantities; none is silently substituted for another.
Soares explicitly questions the simple maternal-Taiwan component of a prior Slow Boat account. The inputs incorrectly collapse differing maternal models into one agreement.
3090–2258 cal BP is a modeled start boundary, not a full closed pottery occupation; possible 3903–3420 cal BP association is tentative.
Shared ancestry does not prove one route or direction. Ioannidis 2021 did not sample Hawaiʻi; the Hawaiʻi review's sampling-limit claim remains canonical.
The input's 'reverse west-to-east' phrase is geographically inconsistent. Actual source assignments and independent population histories are retained without a generic directional arrow.
Kayser 2006 percentages refer to mtDNA/Y marker classifications in studied samples, not whole-genome fractions or resident-population counts.
Cochrane 2005 is Archaeology International, not Artificial Intelligence. It emphasizes limited early mobility evidence rather than mapping all highland trails.

corrections.target: Modern Fiji identity and origin narratives
corrections.correction: Cocom's contemporary mixed-identity interviews and Jones's Biblical genealogical narratives do not establish prehistoric highland tribal genetic origins.

Vanuatu genomic transformations are not automatically Fiji highland ancestry estimates. Feldman 2026 supports distinct Fiji dispersals and a local kin/status association, not one ancestry profile for every highland community.
Ra relocation evidence includes historical/community testimony. The proposed AD 1300 climate mechanism is interpretive and does not prove universal mass flight into fortified highlands.

corrections.target: Sourced phases versus static period labels
corrections.correction: Site phases and century-level abstract dating are approximate. Lapita, Archaic or Ceramic labels do not independently assign languages, ethnicities, precise settlement endpoints or resident numbers.

corrections.correction: Tuck 1971 is a review of George F. MacDonald’s 1968 excavation monograph. It is not the original field report. Calibrated chronology here follows Lothrop et al. 2016 Table 3; firsthand observations use Stuckenrath 1964.

Debert 10,600 ± 47 radiocarbon BP is distinguished from its published 12,630 ± 135 cal BP summary. Labrador 7530 ± 140 BP and 8600 ± 325 BP remain unplaced without an independently verified calibration.

corrections.issue: A pooled date is not an occupation duration
corrections.correction: Debert’s displayed interval is the published 2σ summary translated from calendar BP, not an occupation lasting throughout the interval. The pooled suite count differs between the review and older accounts.
Cowpath’s legacy age is not copied to Cowpath East or Cowpath West. The combined Iceberg / Black Rock Brook sequence is not assigned as each site’s occupation span.

corrections.issue: Historical continuity and causation model overstated
corrections.correction: McGhee and Tuck’s proposed local development and possible environmental / Dorset-related change remain interpretive hypotheses, not demonstrated genetic continuity or single-cause displacement.

corrections.issue: Pacific comparisons presented as Atlantic evidence
corrections.correction: Pacific raised shorelines, submerged deposits, footprints, LIDAR screening and watercraft least-cost models do not establish an Atlantic migration route. Model scenarios and environmental opportunities remain distinct from observed human presence.
Use the primary conclusion’s 13,317–12,633 cal BP associated-wood envelope. The track-makers are a minimum of three individuals, not a resident population census.
Primary author CV and DOI metadata give pages 64–108; supplied 108–164 is not retained.
Original MA thesis, preliminary field report and later published chapter are separate works. The thesis year remains unresolved between 1984 and 1985 in accessed bibliographies.

corrections.issue: One-page notices and book reviews used as original analyses
corrections.correction: Tuck 1978 and the Works in Stone review do not provide independently accessed field methods or a local archaeological chronology.

corrections.issue: Uncontacted is not a synonym for Indigenous Amazonian
corrections.correction: Sampled Waorani, Ashaninka, Tikuna, Pano and other communities cannot stand for all peoples now avoiding sustained contact. Source-specific sampling and consent distinguish the categories.
Founder/drift examples coexist with high diversity and intergroup connections in other samples; neither pattern applies uniformly to Amazonia.
Maternal/paternal lineage common-ancestor ages do not date a people, a language, an archaeological occupation or a specific travel route. Original kya retained without unverified cal-BP conversion.
Di Corcia2017 reports a marker-specific interpretation of limited exchange, not permanent cultural isolation, zero ancestry from every outside population, or present uncontacted status.

The inspected abstract reports 157 Amazonian mitogenomes including Indigenous, European and African ancestry and reference-assignment limitations. It does not establish a sample of uncontacted groups; urban recruitment also not asserted without methods.

Skoglund2015 models differentiated Native American founding ancestry; neither it nor Castro e Silva2026 directly observes an Australian voyage or establishes the language/identity of a hypothesized source.

Walker2023 ecological-footprint/fire trends are indirect demographic proxies, potentially influenced by tools and detection; absence of a detectable clearing is not proof of abandonment, extinction or an empty forest.

Eastern Tukanoan/Arawakan marriage contact is a described cultural practice. It is not genetic proof of linguistic descent, and language affiliations of unsampled voluntarily isolated groups remain unknown.
'OUP accepted manuscript' resolves to Castro e Silva et al., Population Histories and Genomic Diversity of South American Natives, MBE39(1), msab339; online December2021, issue2022.
Primary PDF heading states Human Heredity2001;51:79–84, correcting RIS2000.
Online2020 and volume51 issue2021 are distinguished; no historical event date derives from either.
Human Biology86(2):93–104, correcting input104–93.
Barbieri bioRxiv505628 is the precursor to msz174; Harris bioRxiv219808 is the precursor to PNAS1720798115. These paired references are not independent studies.
Both complete PDFs read; all18+50 RIS rows logged across56 distinct DOI entries, including comparative/deferred sources omitted from the short report bibliographies.

sourceRegister.title: How did Lapita-related admixture and later Austronesian gene flow shape Fiji Highlands?
sourceRegister.access: All five pages extracted with pypdf and read, including text, phase table, figure captions and 13-item bibliography. No copied figure image treated as new field data.
sourceRegister.note: The PDF identifies Consensus as its synthesis tool. Root archives the original file and complete extraction; this sidecar records reviewed facts only. No deployment authorized.

unresolved: No cited primary evidence reviewed here establishes a uniform 70–90% Papuan-related genome-wide ancestry proportion for Viti Levu highland groups. Obtain community-specific sampling, model definitions and tables before any such estimate.
Feldman (2026) full-text download failed. Its abstract supports distinct Fiji dispersals and a status/kinship association in one community, not a highland-wide lineage or climatic-isolation sequence.

The synopsis phase ranges 3000–2700, 2500–2000 and 2000–1200 BP are not accepted as synchronized Fiji highland occupation/genetic events. Model ages, sample dates and ceramic horizons need separate contextual chronologies.

AD 1300–1700 fortification and AD 1000–1800 Polynesian back-flow ranges need explicit local dates and archaeological/genomic evidence. Cochrane abstract alone does not supply them; Skoglund (2016) does not test AD 1300 climate-driven relocation.

The assertion that later Tongan voyagers strongly reshaped eastern Fiji while western highland clans remained isolated is not established by the accessed sources. No exact route, tribe boundary or ancestry gradient added.
Liu (2026) Palau dating depends on radiocarbon dietary/reservoir assumptions and model generation time. No fresh calibration performed and no detailed dated Palauan site distribution added.

Posth (2018) incremental process and Lipson (2018)/2020 demographic interpretations must remain separately attributed. Broad agreement on ancestry transformation does not settle its tempo or exact source-route history.

RIS semantic identity with existing Fiedel (2000) bibliography is confirmed; historical byte-for-byte identity cannot be established without the previous-upload checksum. Its 390 entries are references, not 390 reviewed studies.
corrections: The PDF question concerns Fiji highlands, but its cited populations span Vanuatu, Tonga, Palau, Micronesia and Munda. Findings cannot be transferred simply because all are Oceanian.

Early Vanuatu/Tonga individuals had little detectable Papuan-related ancestry. This does not demonstrate bypass of every Near Oceanian community or absence of early admixture throughout Remote Oceania; Palau differs.

Feldman (2026) later Polynesian-related gene flow around a millennium ago specifically concerns southern Vanuatu Outlier communities in the abstract; it does not independently date Fiji highland back-migration.
Isshiki (2020) sampled Munda, Solomon Islands. Elevated Papuan-related HLA local ancestry and proposed selection are not Fiji-highland genome-wide ancestry or direct proof of one endemic pathogen.
The reproduced Skoglund Extended Data Figure 3 shows Tongan admixture dates and Figure 4 models a 25% contribution to Tongans. New Guinean Highlander proxy is not a sample of Fiji highlanders.
Liu (2022) supports a Micronesian matrilocality interpretation. Matrilocal residence is not matrilineal descent or demonstrated uniform Pacific social organization.
Cochrane (2017) is a book chapter, now verified at Oxford, not an independently dated fortification survey. Burley (2013) is an argued polygenesis model; retain qualifications.
Lipson (2018) journal/preprint identifiers and Matisoo-Smith/Robins (2004) authorship corrected in the register. Rat mitochondrial genealogy is not human genomic admixture.
Fiedel (2000) RIS matches existing American-peopling bibliography context. It is unrelated to Fiji field evidence and is not the full Fiedel paper; no automatic new archaeological claim follows.
No resident counts, precisely bounded settlement/distribution dates, exact voyage paths, archaeological coordinates or language-divergence ages are inferred from these summaries.

unresolved: Obtain the complete Parkhill article and modern site chronology before accepting the synthesis’s Grid B hearth, pollen association, Folsom-like production and numerical age claims; the Hipwater Parkhill-phase record is a different locality.
Obtain Lepper/Tankersley chapters and exact outcrop or workshop records before creating Walhonding/Upper Mercer individual sites or dated procurement routes.
Obtain the complete Brown–Vierra Koster chapter and primary horizon dates. The eHRAF 8300–4900 BP coverage range is indexing context, not one uninterrupted local occupation.
Identify the correct archaeological Wall Ridge reference; do not silently replace Jill Duncan with an unrelated similarly named author.
Check full Jones dissertation stratigraphy, dating and alternative interpretations before assigning a numerical Carson-Conn-Short occupation interval.
For Coats-Hines-Litchy, review the original proposed age/association and later reevaluations together before presenting the full dispute; no early dated occupation added here.
Coordinates were not verified in the accessible sources. New records retain named fuzzy regional context and null geometry rather than precise site points.
Lambert metadata carries a 2025 volume/year and 2026 copyright note; retain repository citation year while leaving exact online chronology unresolved.
Full publisher text for several papers returned 403. Prior-source access notes are distinguished from new abstract/metadata review; no claim of reading inaccessible article bodies.
corrections: Krus 2019 dates Lawrenz Gun Club’s Mississippian phase, not the beginning of Midwest occupation around 13,000 cal BP. Its model intervals are kept separate from early Paleoindian evidence.

Belson already exists. Talbot 2021 is the relevant initial publication; the supplied attribution of its site details to Lothrop 2016 is not accepted as a direct site-dating reference. Nash 2024 still flags dating work pending.

Duncan 2020 is a Book review in History of Education Review, not a verified Wall Ridge excavation source. Exclude the asserted early-1300s Wall Ridge earthlodge and crop claims until the correct reference is obtained.

Jones 2018 is a doctoral dissertation, not a journal article. Its regional 13,200–10,000 yrs BP cannot become a calibrated Carson-Conn-Short site span; continuous residence remains an attributed interpretation.
Roosa is the missing author of the 1977 Parkhill paper (349–354). Parkhill is in Ontario, not a US site. Its 10,750–9,750 BP range is not relabelled cal BP or converted to BCE.
Brown and Vierra is a 1983 book chapter, reissued electronically in 2016; its supplied DOI is book-level. It appears in both RIS lists and is not two independent studies.
Tankersley and Lepper are book chapters, despite RIS JOUR tags; electronic metadata dates are not occupation ages.
235 Missouri/Iowa points are an artifact inventory, not 235 sites or people. Regional distribution does not establish continuous residence at any unnamed locus.
Legg’s existing predictive regional model is not an inventory of newly confirmed settlements or a proven migration route.

The Neolithic synthesis omits Woodland from its main sequence and overstates a universal prohibition on the term. Use region-specific Paleoindian, Archaic, Woodland, Mississippian, Oneota/Huber and Plains Village terminology where supported, without mapping them one-to-one onto Neolithic.
Cultivation, pottery and sedentism need not first appear together in Late Prehistoric societies. American Bottom antecedents extend into earlier regional periods.

Middle Grant Creek’s single-component early-seventeenth-century description cannot date Knoll Springs or all Langford/Huber occupations; no exact date, population, maize intensity or storage quantity inferred.

unresolved: Full texts and underlying site datasets remain needed for Jones, Raab, Benson, Gardner, Briere and other abstract/metadata-only entries before adding finer site histories.
Foster/Choice bibliographic identity requires verification; no southeastern abandonment, buffer-zone or river relocation claims accepted from this item or the Barnes review.
Galloway and Pei are broad comparative works; verify study population and geographic coverage before applying them to specific Indigenous North American communities.
No exact archaeological coordinates or population totals were verified for new regional records; both remain absent.
No individual Northeast migrant origins, destinations or refuge population estimates were established in the source scope accessed.
corrections: The headline that medieval megadroughts drove continent-wide depopulation turns correlation and regional hypotheses into a universal causal fact. Climate effects are spatially variable and mediated by institutions, subsistence and social relations.
Stager documents severe Northeast droughts around 1260–1330 and 1360–1390. The synthesis’s settled hydroclimatic-refuge and migrant-absorption narrative is not accepted.
Friesen explicitly finds no warming link for Thule expansion around 1250; social drivers are preferred. Late Dorset expansion and later Inuit southern redistribution are separate episodes.
Bird’s abandonment interval extends to 1450 and is staggered. It must not be compressed into a universal 1200s collapse or used to override Cahokia site chronology.
Benson drought intervals are discrete; no continuous drought from 990 to 1297, complete Fremont/Ancestral Pueblo abandonment everywhere, or automatic high mortality is established.
McCool uses settlement defensibility as a conflict proxy and models interacting social/climatic variables; it is not direct proof of warfare at every settlement.

Gardner is a 2005 UNLV dissertation, not a 2019 journal paper. Kelly is print 2013 with 2012 online publication; McCool is volume 91 (2026) with 2025 online publication; Briere prairie-forest is volume 41 (2023), despite 2022 supplied metadata.
Barnes is a book review, not Cable’s primary monograph. Foster’s Choice DOI is unresolved and not accepted as a primary site source.
Doering is already represented by alaska-doering-climate-counterpoint; the repeat citation is not a new independent finding or evidence for a Thule warming narrative.

unresolved: Bolnick full text was inaccessible through the attempted primary endpoint. The 40.4% variance comparison is not independently verified and is omitted from accepted findings; even a valid AMOVA comparison would not prove language descent.
No universal 8,000–10,000-year ceiling for comparative linguistics is accepted from this synopsis; dating and recoverability depend on evidence and methods.
No chapter-level count of families versus isolates was checked. “Around 50 families and numerous isolates” risks conflating categories and is not used.
Brown’s supplied DOI remains unresolved independently; the publisher title, authors, year and scope were verified through its book page.

Greenhill’s abstract age range is a model estimate; its reference year and full calibration assumptions were not checked, so no calendar conversion or closed language-distribution interval is assigned.
corrections: Na-Dené and proposed Dene–Yeniseian relationship are not equivalent levels of classification. The PDF’s “linked by consensus” and “confirm” wording is replaced by attributed model language.
Urban and Guzmán Naranjo investigate a continental structural gradient; that result is not a demonstration of Dene–Yeniseian descent or an observed migration.
Greenhill’s northern Uto-Aztecan origin is one model, not a disproof of every southern or agricultural scenario. Preserve the existing Nakatsuka alternative and distinguish genes from language.
Greenhill pages are 81–107, not RIS 107–181 or PDF 107–81. Institutional DOI is 10.1353/lan.2023.0006; supplied 10.1353/lan.0.0276 remains in provenance.
10.2307/417069 identifies Doris Bartholomew’s 1999 review of Campbell’s 1997 book, not a Campbell-authored 1999 original study.
Thomason’s handbook review belongs to Language 82(4), December 2006, not 2007.
Kilarski and Silver–Miller are books, although the RIS labels them JOUR; Brown author initials are expanded from publisher metadata.
Brown’s book proposes Aleut–Utian and challenges familiar affiliations; its publisher description cannot be recast as general consensus support for the synopsis family table.
Ward’s historical use of Amerind and placement of Haida in Na-Dene are not adopted. Sicoli–Holton explicitly treat Haida as an unrelated isolate outgroup.
Typological traits, genetic correlations, language family membership and community identities are separate evidence categories. No family is assigned to ancient genomic samples.

Synopsis suppresses very large uncertainty: external governmental table lists 8475 ±650 RCYBP among multiple problematic dates. Do not plot 8475 as a secure exact calendar occupation age; obtain original dating discussion.
Reservoir Lakes, Cloquet Lake, Misiano/McDougal Lake, Big Rice Lake and Eveleth retained as leads only until primary site descriptions and dating are checked.

Anderson and Gillam 2000; Darvill 2018; Beaudoin 1996; Horta 2019 and other register entries without added claims require targeted primary review before additional site facts. Horta concerns Argentina and cannot establish North American shoreline occupation.

corrections.correction: No uniform 26–13.8 ka blockage or compulsory coastal itinerary is established here. Different sectors, physical access, ecology, and archaeological use require separate claims.

Woywitka 11.3 ±0.8 ka uses 2010 CE IRSL datum; the synopsis incorrectly labels it cal BP and conflates post-flood sediment with arrival and flood dates. Lesnek 2018 is not an Athabasca flood excavation source.
10,000–5,000 14C BP components do not establish continuous occupation; retained raw, not subtracted from 1950.
Coastal accessibility and model compatibility are not proof that all initial populations used a single coastal route.
Genetic bison movements are not evidence proving a human migration in the same direction.
